title: Chest-Supported Row
summary: A row with your chest on a pad: upper back 1, lats 0.7, rear delts 0.6. The pad takes the lower back out of the lift.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine) or adjustable (incline) bench; commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine) or dumbbells.

muscles.why: Rhomboids and mid traps pull the shoulder blades together; a horizontal row lines up with them best.
The lats pull the upper arm back (shoulder extension); elbows kept close to the body give them more work.
The rear delts pull the upper arm back, more with the elbows flared out.
Mid and lower traps squeeze the shoulder blades; rated 0.5.
The elbow flexors bend the elbows; helper (0.4).

setup.text: Set the chest pad so the handles are reachable with straight arms.
Chest on the pad, feet planted.
Choose the grip: neutral and close for more lats, wide for more upper back.

form_cues.cue: Keep your chest on the pad
form_cues.why: Starting with the shoulder blades moving keeps the upper back doing the work.

form_cues.cue: Row the elbows back past your torso
form_cues.why: Keeping the chest on the pad means the legs and lower back stay out of it.
Full arm extension stretches the upper back.

form_cues.cue: Pause a moment with the elbows back
form_cues.why: The upper back is shortest there; it is easy to cut short.

bias_tweaks.change: Wide grip, elbows flared to about 60-80 degrees
bias_tweaks.effect: Moves the pull toward horizontal abduction, more upper back and rear delt.
More shoulder extension, more lat work.
bias_tweaks.caveat: The lats still help in both.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Lifting the chest off the pad to cheat the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest on the pad; lighten the load if you have to lift off it.

mistakes.text: Lifting the chest off the pad to finish reps.
mistakes.fix: That turns it into a cheated row.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.

misconceptions.myth: Machines don't build muscle like free weights.
misconceptions.reality: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth in a meta-analysis. Pick by fit, stability and how well you can push close to failure.

misconceptions.myth: You must squeeze for 2 seconds at the top for the upper back to grow.
misconceptions.reality: A short pause helps control the range; a long hold isn't required. Tempo changes growth little.

lower_risk.text: The app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the first working load is at least 40 kg (95 lb) and the main muscle is not already warm from an earlier lift. Otherwise start with a slightly lighter first set.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 8-12 rep range. With the chest supported, you can push close to failure without the lower back being a limit.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Cable row with more lat work (lats 0.8).
One arm at a time; more range for the lats.
Same idea on an incline bench with dumbbells.
Lying on a high bench with a barbell; heavier loads and still no lower back.

notes: Row variations have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites; grip choices are biomechanics.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
